title: Giving Context to AI: How to Write Better Prompts
introduction: Providing the right background, audience, and constraints helps an AI give useful and accurate answers. This lesson shows how to add just the right context to your prompts.

sections.heading: Why Context Matters
sections.subheading: How background information improves AI responses
paragraphs: AI models generate answers based on the information you give them. When you add relevant context, the model can focus on what matters most.
Without context, the response may be vague or miss key details that you need.

example.title: Chatbot answering a travel question
example.content: Without context: "Tell me about Paris." With context: "I am planning a 3‑day family trip to Paris in June. We like museums and kid‑friendly activities. Suggest an itinerary that fits our budget of $1500."

sections.heading: Choosing Relevant Background
sections.subheading: Picking details that help the AI understand the task
paragraphs: Identify the facts that directly affect the answer, such as dates, locations, or specific subjects. These are the pieces of background the AI needs.
Leave out unrelated history or personal stories that do not change the result.

example.title: Summarizing a news article
example.content: Relevant context: "Summarize the Reuters article published on 12 Oct 2023 about the new electric car policy in Germany. Highlight the main goals and expected impact."

sections.heading: Separating Useful from Irrelevant
sections.subheading: Avoiding extra details that confuse the AI
paragraphs: Extra information can distract the model and lead to longer or off‑topic replies. Keep the prompt focused on what will influence the answer.
If a detail does not change the outcome, it is better left out.

example.title: Writing a recipe prompt
example.content: Useful context: "Give me a gluten‑free chocolate cake recipe for 8 people, using only ingredients I have: flour, cocoa powder, eggs, butter, sugar." Irrelevant detail: "I love baking on rainy Sundays."

sections.heading: Specifying Audience and Situation
sections.subheading: Tailoring responses for who will read them
paragraphs: State who will use the answer – a child, a manager, a teacher – so the AI can adjust tone and complexity.
Mention the situation, such as a presentation, a report, or a casual chat, to guide the style.

example.title: Explaining a concept to different audiences
example.content: For a child: "Explain photosynthesis in simple words with a fun example." For a scientist: "Provide a detailed biochemical pathway of photosynthesis, including electron transport chain specifics."

sections.heading: Building a Context‑Rich Prompt
sections.subheading: Putting all pieces together in a clear format
paragraphs: Combine background, audience, goal, and constraints in a logical order. Use short sentences and bullet‑like structure if helpful.
A well‑structured prompt saves time and produces the answer you expect.

example.title: Prompt for a marketing plan
example.content: "I run a small online store selling handmade candles. My target audience is eco‑conscious adults aged 25‑40. Create a 3‑month marketing plan that includes social media ideas, email campaigns, and a budget not exceeding $2000."

practice.title: Create Your Own Context Prompt
practice.instruction: Write a short prompt for an AI to help you plan a weekend trip. Include the destination, who you are traveling with, your budget, and any special interests such as hiking or museums.

keyTakeaways: Relevant background guides the AI to give precise answers.
Only include details that affect the result; omit unrelated information.
State the audience and situation so the AI can match tone and style.
Combine background, goal, audience, and constraints in a clear order.
A concise, context‑rich prompt leads to faster and more useful responses.

mcqs.question: What is most likely to happen when a prompt does not include relevant background information?
options: The AI will generate a highly detailed response covering many topics.
The AI may produce a vague or incomplete answer that misses key details.
The AI will refuse to answer the question.
The AI will ask for more information before responding.
mcqs.explanation: Without context, the model lacks guidance and often returns a vague or incomplete answer, as described in the lesson.

mcqs.question: When asking the AI to summarize a news article about a new electric car policy in Germany, which detail is most essential?
options: The publication date of the article.
The author's favorite car brand.
The weather on the day the article was published.
The length of the article in words.
mcqs.explanation: The lesson emphasizes that dates are relevant background facts that directly affect the summary.

mcqs.question: In the recipe prompt example, which piece of information is considered irrelevant?
options: The list of ingredients needed.
The number of servings (8 people).
The requirement for a gluten‑free cake.
"I love baking on rainy Sundays."
mcqs.explanation: Personal preferences that do not affect the recipe outcome are irrelevant and should be omitted.

mcqs.question: To get an explanation of photosynthesis suitable for a child, which instruction should be included in the prompt?
options: Provide a detailed biochemical pathway of photosynthesis.
Include statistical data and citations.
Explain photosynthesis in simple words with a fun example.
Use technical jargon appropriate for researchers.
mcqs.explanation: Specifying the audience (a child) tells the AI to use simple language and a fun example, matching the lesson on audience tailoring.

mcqs.question: Which ordering best follows the recommended structure for a context‑rich prompt?
options: Goal, background, audience, constraints.
Audience, constraints, background, goal.
Constraints, goal, audience, background.
Background, audience, goal, constraints.
mcqs.explanation: The lesson advises combining background, audience, goal, and constraints in that logical order.
